name: 370 mm scale test, 3 mm gap
notes: The geometry that motivated graded meshing: a 370 mm outer diameter with a 3 mm air gap, the proportions of a YASA-class axial-flux machine. Three cells across that gap means ~1 mm cells across a ~520 mm box, which is about 116 million uniform cells; a uniform grid cannot do this at any practical size. Note this is a scale test of the mesh and solver, not a model of a YASA motor: the topology here is still the PCB coreless stator with a low-permeability salient-pole rotor, because permanent magnets and high-mu steel are outside what the reduced scalar potential can currently represent (see docs/limitations.md).
